# fx-report — the REPORTER seat (host-side, agent-unwritable, a function
# of observable system state; design record §1a/§7.1).  Machine records
# are the non-'#' lines: tab-separated, frozen column order per tag.
# Every record is marked MEASURED / DERIVED / ABSENT, and every ABSENT
# says WHICH kind of absence it is.  The taxonomy and retention tables
# below are printed on every run — they are the grammar, not commentary.
taxonomy	activation	fxstore snapshots + facts:generation per version (every publish IS a snapshot)	absence=none-occurred (within what survived gc --retain / renumber; a pruned activation is absence=not-recorded-ANYMORE)
taxonomy	activation-input	facts:generation_config(genhash,sha,origin) + the retained copy <store>/<origin> (fx-init 1399dbd)	no-fact=absent-pre-link (a store-bootstrap snapshot or a pre-1399dbd activation: legitimate); fact+copy-gone=FINDING (the input is no longer readable)
taxonomy	boot-verdict	<store>/.bootlog line <v> ok|failed <epoch> <nonce> (fx-init bootlog_append)	no-.bootlog=no-boot-ever-recorded; .bootlog-with-no-failed=none-failed-within-what-the-log-retains (the log is append-only and never pruned by the store)
taxonomy	boot-start	<store>/.bootlog line <v> in-progress <epoch> <nonce>	a boot that started; a version with no line never started a recorded boot
taxonomy	shutdown	<store>/.bootlog line <v> shutdown <epoch> <nonce> (the SIGTERM path only)	absence=no-RECORDED-clean-shutdown (a crash is indistinguishable from never shutting down — the log cannot say 'no shutdown happened')
taxonomy	roll-forward-automatic	<store>/.recovery data row <epoch> <published> <from-failed> <genhash> <nonce> (fx-init, once per successful roll-forward)	no-file=no-automatic-roll-forward-ever-recorded; no-row-naming-v=v-was-not-published-by-the-automatic-path (within the file's retention)
taxonomy	operator-intervention	MEASURED — <store>/.operator rows: one line per intervention on the generation plane, written by PID1's control handler (fx-init ca9cb06) or, since the runtime-record closure, by fx-activate ITSELF for a publish it committed OUTSIDE that handler on a boot carrying an fx.bootnonce= (the file's own OPERATOR_HEADER, operator_journal.zig:122, IS the definition — ONE definition, imported by both writers): <epoch> <action> <arg> <outcome> <from-version|-> <to-version|-> <boot-nonce|none>, appended + fsync'd BEFORE the reply is flushed (operator_append: shutdown :3556, activate-failed :3665, unverified :3705, refused-config :3730, dhake-failed :3816, ok :3829, rollback unverified :3849, refused :3858, refused-config :3877, ok :3920).  SECOND WRITER (the runtime-record closure): fx-activate records the publish IT committed OUTSIDE that handler — one row, activate/ok or activate/unverified, on a boot carrying an fx.bootnonce= — through the SAME grammar and header (selfRecord, fx-init activate.zig:898/:1769/:1755; the writer itself, operator_journal.zig:235).  action = the ctrl arm that wrote it, arg = the operator's operand VERBATIM, outcome = ok | failed:<rc> | refused | refused-config | dhake-failed | unverified.  The journal records the GENERATION PLANE ONLY — its header names what it does NOT record (the reads, file transfers, the shell, per-service commands, probe) and what it cannot record AND cannot DETECT: the paths that bypass PID1's handler (host-side `fxstore rollback`, `rollback --hard`, a hand-edited CURRENT).  DERIVED — the RETAINED FALLBACK, for a store with NO .operator and for exactly those bypass paths: two signatures. (restore) version r whose genhash matches a version TWO-OR-MORE back (a duplicate of only the IMMEDIATELY-PRECEDING generation is fx-activate's own publish-of-live — MEASURED: every activation after the first leaves that benign pair — or gc's publish-first, and is NOT this class) and no .recovery row publishes r — the ctrl rollback arm (init.zig:3853) and host `fxstore rollback` drive the SAME soft rollback and append NOTHING to .recovery; (current-repoint) CURRENT != newest. Both are DERIVED, never a verdict.	TWO DIFFERENT STATES, never conflated: (i) .operator PRESENT with zero rows = no generation-plane intervention in the retained journal — a MEASUREMENT, not a gap; (ii) .operator ABSENT = a store PREDATING ca9cb06 (or one never booted under it) — NOT 'none occurred' (see absence/.operator).  For (ii), and for the bypass paths the journal's own header lists as NOT-RECORDED-AND-NOT-DETECTABLE, the DERIVED signature is the fallback and it is a DISJUNCTION: an operator rollback OR a deliberate re-activation of an older config — either way content moved back without the automatic .recovery row — OR a removed .recovery row, which the AUDIT seat's previous-observation comparison, not this seat, is built to catch.  The derived signature is only a backward move or a stale CURRENT, and gc/renumber can destroy both.  A journal row does NOT suppress the derived row: it can EXPLAIN a backward move but cannot prove the journal saw every path that produced one.
taxonomy	activation-refusal	MEASURED — <store>/.operator rows whose outcome is a refusal (fx-init ca9cb06): failed:<rc> (the activate executor exited rc; nothing landed — init.zig:3665), refused-config (the generation DID land in the store but PID1 REFUSED it — the declared service set past its bound, or a configuration read_store_facts could not read: :3730 from the activate arm, :3877 from the rollback arm, the writer's own 'same durable record from the other direction'), refused (the STORE rejected a rollback target — :3858).  Recorded in the SAME journal and NOT this class: dhake-failed (:3816 — the generation DID land, the live-root reapply failed) and unverified (:3705 — the store could not be re-opened to confirm, i.e. AMBIGUOUS, which is not the same as refused).  The tmpfs runtime log that held these (rt_effect activate failed|dhake-failed, init.zig:3667/:3818, DEFAULT_RUN :32) still dies at every reboot and is NOT read by this seat.	no-row-with-a-refusal-outcome-in-the-retained-journal = no RECORDED refusal within the journal (a count of RECORDED refusals, never of attempts).  This absence-meaning WAS 'NOT-DURABLY-RECORDED' before ca9cb06 — a refused activation left NOTHING in the store (fx-activate refuses before touching it) and PID1's record of it lived in /run's tmpfs — and it is that again EXACTLY WHEN .operator IS ABSENT: a store predating the journal CANNOT answer this class, and the report says so via absence/.operator instead of printing a zero.  Bounds carried INTO the class: a REFUSAL row is written by PID1's control handler alone (a direct exec records only a publish that reached commit), so an fx-activate that refuses outside that handler is invisible; `unverified` rows are ambiguity, not refusals; and root in-guest can forge or truncate the file exactly as it can .bootlog — a row is CHECKABLE against the store's version/genhash history, not authoritative over it.
taxonomy	content-recurrence	DERIVED: .recovery data rows whose trailing genhash is IDENTICAL (the .recovery header's own semantics: the same content re-failing)	no-repeated-genhash=no-recurrence-within-the-surviving-rows
retention	snapshots (versions+facts)	<store>/.db/snapshots/<v>/ (the disk store)	survives (disk)	survives (a roll-forward PUBLISHES a new version)	NOT-surviving: `fxstore gc --retain N` prunes at publish; after `rollback --hard` a later publish renumbers from CURRENT+1 (the gc --retain guard's own statement, store.zig) and can destroy the versions between	DECIDED (user, 2026-10-12): UNBOUNDED by default — `gc --retain N` is the OPERATOR's deliberate knob and NOTHING SETS IT, the same decision as the journals below: every published version survives unless an operator asks otherwise (§1a gap 4 is now this DECISION, not a gap)
retention	.bootlog	<store>/.bootlog (fx-init, append-only, fsync+syncfs per append)	survives (disk)	survives (append)	survives (fxstore does not know the file; it outlives pruned versions)	DECIDED (user, 2026-10-12): UNBOUNDED, and NOTHING MAY BE DROPPED — bootlog_last/bootlog_newest_ok_below need the newest `ok` below CURRENT (that IS the roll-forward TARGET), and fx-audit's append accounting + its previous-observation comparison need the record INTACT (a rotation reads as a REWRITE of a previously observed record and fires on a HEALTHY machine).  Growth is linear in events that really happened: the guardrail bounds it to real boots, one in-progress line per in-guest activation and one verdict per boot.  THE STATED COST, not hidden: the file is FULLY RESCANNED on every boot (bootlog_last/bootlog_newest_ok_below), so per-boot work is linear in its length (§1a gap 4 is now this DECISION, not a gap)
retention	.recovery	<store>/.recovery (fx-init, '#'-header + one data row per automatic roll-forward)	survives (disk)	survives (append)	survives (fxstore does not know the file)	DECIDED (user, 2026-10-12): UNBOUNDED, and NOTHING MAY BE DROPPED — one row per AUTOMATIC roll-forward and the record stays INTACT (fx-audit's append accounting + its previous-observation comparison: a rotation reads as a REWRITE of a previously observed record and fires on a HEALTHY machine).  Growth is linear in roll-forwards that really happened (§1a gap 4 is now this DECISION, not a gap)
retention	retained config (the INPUT)	<store>/<genhash>-system-generation/config.dhall (fx-activate, per activation)	survives (disk)	survives (each activation writes its own gen dir)	RETAINED-WHILE-NAMED (MEASURED on this tree, store.zig pinned blob 30dce7cb: `fxstore gc <root>` keeps every <genhash>-system-generation dir named by a SURVIVING snapshot's generation fact — the dir sweep's carve-out, logged per dir on stderr; a dir whose snapshot was pruned by `gc --retain N` IS reaped, with its facts)	DECIDED (user, 2026-10-12): UNBOUNDED by default — no pruning-by-age policy exists to state, because the copy is exactly as durable as the snapshot that names it (`gc --retain N` prunes version and dir together, and NOTHING sets that default): retention is bounded only by an operator's deliberate gc, never by time.  A GENUINELY missing copy (hand-deleted, or a dir a surviving fact names that is gone) still fires config-retained-copy-gone
retention	.operator	<store>/.operator (fx-init ca9cb06, '#'-header + one data row per intervention on the generation plane — a control-channel REQUEST (appended+fsync'd by the handler BEFORE the reply is flushed, INCLUDING the ones that FAILED or were REFUSED) or, since the runtime-record closure, ONE row for a publish fx-activate committed OUTSIDE the handler on a boot carrying an fx.bootnonce= (a self-recorded row never carries "none"))	survives (disk)	survives (append — one row per ctrl request whatever its outcome, plus one per direct-exec publish where the boot carries a nonce)	survives (fxstore does not know the file; it outlives pruned versions AND keeps rows naming versions gc has since pruned — a row records the move the operator asked for, it is not a promise the version is still there)	DECIDED (user, 2026-10-12): UNBOUNDED, and NOTHING MAY BE DROPPED — one row per control-channel intervention and fx-audit's append accounting + its previous-observation comparison need the record INTACT (a rotation reads as a REWRITE of a previously observed record and fires on a HEALTHY machine).  Growth is linear in interventions that really happened, whose rate is the OPERATOR's own (§1a gap 4 is now this DECISION, not a gap).  NOT tamper-proof: PID1's control handler owns it and fx-activate adds one row for a publish committed outside that handler on a boot carrying a nonce (its TWO writers, in the file's own header), but root in-guest can forge or truncate it exactly as it can .bootlog
retention	runtime datalog rt_effect/rt_control	/run/fx/log.db (fx-init init.zig:33 DEFAULT_RUN; path built :4856, opened :4857 by fx_log_open) — read by NOBODY here	DOES NOT SURVIVE (post-pivot '/' is tmpfs, init.zig M4 pivot — the log dies at every reboot)	n/a (dies with the boot that wrote it)	n/a	death-by-construction for the RUNTIME view only: the tmpfs log holds the live ctrl/effect stream, but every operator intervention it carried (activate, refused activate, dhake-failed, rollback, shutdown) is durably recorded SINCE fx-init ca9cb06 in <store>/.operator — and this seat reads THAT, never /run. What survives is what .bootlog/.recovery/.operator/snapshots hold/snapshots
retention	CURRENT	<store>/.db/snapshots/CURRENT (atomic tmp+rename per publish/rollback)	survives (disk)	rewritten per publish (the roll-forward's own CURRENT)	kept (gc --retain REFUSES a non-newest CURRENT rather than prune it)	-
bound	rt-log-tmpfs	the runtime datalog's live ctrl/effect stream (activations, refused activations, rollbacks, shutdowns) lived at /run/fx/log.db and is GONE at every reboot (tmpfs post-pivot) — this report never reads it.  Since fx-init ca9cb06 those same interventions are ALSO written durably to <store>/.operator, and THIS seat reads that file instead (operator_append is called BEFORE the reply is flushed, so the row outlives a machine killed right after the answer).  The bound is therefore now a property of the STORE, not of the report: without .operator (a store predating the journal) nothing durable can say whether an activation was refused.
bound	pre-first-snapshot	nothing before the store's first snapshot is representable; a .bootlog line naming a version not in the timeline is reported as such (pruned by gc, or written by a store history this disk no longer holds)
bound	operator-journal-bounds	<store>/.operator is the durable operator record SINCE fx-init ca9cb06, and it is bounded on every side: it holds the GENERATION PLANE only, and only what PID1's control handler saw — plus, since the RUNTIME-RECORD CLOSURE, the publishes fx-activate committed OUTSIDE that handler (a direct exec: the harness's channel-less fallback, or a command in the interactive shell) on a boot carrying an fx.bootnonce=, ONE row each and only when the publish REACHED COMMIT (a pre-publish failure records nothing: there is no request to attribute it to).  The file's own header (OPERATOR_HEADER, operator_journal.zig:122) names what it does NOT record — the reads (status/q/grep/search), file transfers (put/rm), per-service commands (start/stop/restart), probe, and a malformed request no arm executed; the `shell` REQUEST is still not recorded, although a DIRECT exec FROM that shell now records its own publish — and what is NOT recorded AND NOT DETECTABLE: a host-side `fxstore rollback`, `rollback --hard`, a hand-edited store CURRENT.  Root in-guest can forge or truncate the file exactly as it can .bootlog: a row is CHECKABLE against the store's version/genhash history, not authoritative over it.  A store predating the journal has NO file at all — absence of the FILE is a state of the store, never 'no interventions occurred'.
bound	operator-bypass-paths	the paths that bypass PID1's control handler have NO record: host-side `fxstore rollback`, `rollback --hard`, and a hand-edited store CURRENT.  A DIRECT EXEC of fx-activate is no longer one of them — it records its own publish on a boot carrying an fx.bootnonce= (the runtime-record closure) — but that row covers exactly its OWN publish, so these three remain the unrecorded set.  Their only durable trace is a generation move the automatic .recovery row does not attribute, so the DERIVED operator-intervention signature is RETAINED as the fallback for them — and it is a DISJUNCTION: an operator rollback, a deliberate re-activation of an older config, or a REMOVED .recovery row (which the AUDIT seat's previous-observation comparison, not this seat, is built to catch).  A rollback to the content that is ALREADY current moves nothing and is invisible in this class by construction.  A journal row can EXPLAIN a derived backward move; it never suppresses the derived row, because the journal cannot prove it saw every path that produced one.
bound	gc-config-loss	MEASURED on this tree: `fxstore gc <root>` RETAINS every <genhash>-system-generation dir a SURVIVING snapshot's generation fact names (the dir sweep's carve-out) and REAPS a dir whose snapshot was pruned by `gc --retain N` — with its facts, so the pruned generation's input is not reportable at all (the version is gone from the timeline: absence-by-retention, not a finding). config-retained-copy-gone therefore requires a GENUINELY missing copy (a hand-deleted file, or a dir a surviving fact names that is gone) — the post-gc store itself is COHERENT
bound	renumber-after-hard	after `rollback --hard` (CURRENT < newest), a later publish renumbers from CURRENT+1 and can destroy the versions between (stated by the gc --retain guard, store.zig; not reproduced here) — the CURRENT!=newest signature is therefore TRANSIENT, visible only until that next publish
bound	retention-unbounded-by-decision	BY DECISION, NOT BY OMISSION (user, 2026-10-12; §1a gap 4 is now a policy): `.bootlog`, `.recovery` and `.operator` grow WITHOUT BOUND and NOTHING MAY BE DROPPED — `bootlog_last`/`bootlog_newest_ok_below` need the newest `ok` below CURRENT (that IS the roll-forward TARGET), and fx-audit's append accounting + its previous-observation comparison need the record INTACT (a rotation reads as a REWRITE of a previously observed record and would fire on a HEALTHY machine).  Growth is linear in events that really happened: real boots, one in-progress line per in-guest activation, one `.recovery` row per automatic roll-forward, one `.operator` row per intervention.  THE STATED COST, not hidden: `.bootlog` is FULLY RESCANNED on every boot, so per-boot work is linear in its length.  The snapshots keep their knob (`gc --retain N`) and NOTHING sets a default — the same decision
